what: First end-to-end serve of tt-tnt on tt-metal v0.77.0 + vllm-tt-plugin bd150c7

stack.vllm: upstream in venv-vllm-standalone (NOT the tenstorrent/vllm fork)
stack.mesh: P300, both chips of one board

result: Server starts, answers, generates. This pairing had never been run.

finding_1_the_384_model_cannot_be_served.what: episod/tt-tnt (the 384 model) cannot run on this box at all.
finding_1_the_384_model_cannot_be_served.why: It has n_kv_heads=3. A P300 board's minimum topology is 2 chips, so num_devices=2, and the plugin asserts n_kv_heads must be divisible by num_devices. 3 is not.
finding_1_the_384_model_cannot_be_served.and_one_chip_is_not_an_escape: Exposing a single chip fails earlier: tt_cluster.cpp:281 classifies a 1-chip P300 as ClusterType::CUSTOM and TT_FATALs demanding a custom fabric mesh graph descriptor. 1 is not a P300 topology; 2 and 4 are. This is why gozer expands a 1-chip request to the whole board.
finding_1_the_384_model_cannot_be_served.consequence: Every recorded free_running baseline in this directory is for episod/tt-tnt and CANNOT be reproduced on this hardware. They are not a baseline we can compare against any more.
finding_1_the_384_model_cannot_be_served.design_note: kv head counts should be chosen divisible by 2 and 4 if the model is ever to be served on P300 or P300_X2. kv=4 works; kv=3 is a dead end here.

finding_2_the_device_repeats_and_its_own.metric: local repeat rate -- fraction of the first 40 generated tokens already seen in the preceding 4. This is the defect metric, per decode-defect-resolved.json; agreement-with-CPU is not.
finding_2_the_device_repeats_and_its_own.worst_prompt: 'The cat sat on the mat and looked at the' -> 0.80, i.e. 'The cat. The cat. The cat.'
finding_2_the_device_repeats_and_its_own.why_this_comparison_is_valid: Same model, same weights, same prompts, same greedy settings. It is a CPU-vs-device gap, not a cross-model one.
finding_2_the_device_repeats_and_its_own.why_it_is_NOT_a_regression_claim: The recorded post-fix figure of 0.0311 is for the 384 model, which this box cannot serve. Comparing 0.1125 against it would compare two different models. No regression is claimed.
finding_2_the_device_repeats_and_its_own.status: OPEN. The model does not loop on CPU. The device does. Cause unknown.

finding_3_the_plugin_is_exonerated.method: A/B: served the same model, same prompts, on plugin bd150c7 and on c127c17, restarting the server between.
finding_3_the_plugin_is_exonerated.result: Byte-identical. Every per-prompt repeat rate, every agreement count, every first-divergence index.
finding_3_the_plugin_is_exonerated.reading: bd150c7 is not the cause and does not affect this path -- it fixes state-slot remapping for CO-BATCHED requests, and this measurement issues one request at a time. It also shows the serving path is deterministic across restarts.
finding_3_the_plugin_is_exonerated.what_it_leaves: tt-metal v0.77.0's device path, or something older that was never measured on this model.

agreement_with_cpu.note: Recorded for completeness only. Greedy free-running paths diverge benignly under bf16; this project already established agreement is not the defect metric.
